38	 *    dose-log entries and diary notes. The envelope `effective` is the bare date (`2024-10-31`).
39	 *    If the patient later edits or deletes anything on that day, HomeLog publishes a new day page that
40	 *    `supersedes` the old one and restates the whole day.
41	 *
42	 * 2. **My Medicines list.** One item each time the patient saves their medicine list. Holds one
43	 *    `my_med` entry per medicine on the list, including ones marked stopped. Each save restates the
44	 *    whole list and `supersedes` the previous list item. `effective` is the date of the save.
45	 *
46	 * Narrative: on a day page, the narrative is the patient's diary notes for the day, verbatim, one
47	 * paragraph per note. HomeLog adds only the bold time label at the start of each paragraph; the words
48	 * inside the `<ref>` span are exactly what the patient typed (spelling and all). Readings and dose-log
49	 * entries have no narrative. A My Medicines list item has a one-line narrative generated by the app
50	 * ("My Medicines, saved 2 May 2026").
51	 *
52	 * Times: HomeLog stores **wall-clock time as shown on the phone, with no UTC offset and no time-zone
53	 * name** (`"2024-10-31T08:20"`). The app does not know which time zone the phone was in. To place a
54	 * reading on a timeline you need the patient's time zone from somewhere else. Envelope `recorded`
55	 * values are server times in UTC and do carry an offset.

58	 * prescription. A self-reported list can differ from every clinic's list, and that is the point of it.
59	 */

61	/** One entry on a HomeLog day page or My Medicines list. */
62	export type HomeLogEntry = BpReading | GlucoseReading | DoseLog | DiaryNote | MyMed;
63	
64	/**
65	 * Local wall-clock date-time as shown on the patient's phone, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, no seconds, no
66	 * offset, no zone. Not UTC. See the module comment.
67	 */

73

75	  measured_at: LocalDateTime;
76	
77	  /** Systolic pressure, mmHg. */
78	  systolic_mmhg: number;
79	
80	  /** Diastolic pressure, mmHg. */
81	  diastolic_mmhg: number;
82	
83	  /** Pulse rate from the cuff, beats per minute. Absent when typed in and the patient left it blank. */

85	
86	  /**

88	   * - 'cuff_sync': sent by a paired Bluetooth cuff. Values are exactly what the cuff measured.
89	   * - 'typed': typed in by the patient (e.g. cuff not paired, or a reading taken elsewhere such as a

92	   * HomeLog does not detect this.
93	   */
94	  entry_method: 'cuff_sync' | 'typed';
95

97	  arm?: 'left' | 'right';

107	  /**

109	   * unit the meter was set to display at the time.

187	 * `<ref>` span whose id equals this entry's id. The payload holds only the tags the patient picked.
188	 */

191	
192	  /** When the patient wrote the note (not necessarily when the symptom started). Local wall time. */

194	
195	  /**
196	   * Symptom tags the patient picked from HomeLog's list. Empty when the note is not about a symptom.

198	   * 'dizzy', 'tired', 'short_of_breath', 'swelling', 'headache', 'cough', 'pain', 'low_mood', 'other'.

257	/**
258	 * Consumer views: the rows a patient-facing chart application shows for one patient's record at one
259	 * health organization.

280	 *   written, never shift it and never drop it. A plain date is a local date.
281	 * - **Partial dates.** A source date may be only a year (`2019`) or a year and month (`2019-06`). Keep exactly

284	 *   other organizations and without correcting the source. Rows come from structured payload entries; the
285	 *   narrative may help interpret an entry, but is never the only basis for a row.

294	 */

298	 * items that supersede or retract earlier ones.
299	 */

Judgment calls:
- **Counting items:** an item counts when its `recorded` time, converted to America/Chicago, falls on or before `asOf`. Anything superseded or retracted by a counting item is dropped.
- **Medications:** the latest counting My Medicines list is the whole list. A drug missing from it is not reported. I did not attempt interactions between lists, because each save restates everything.
- **Ingredient names:** I take the ingredient from the drug-search display name when there is one, with strength and salt words removed. Otherwise I use a built-in brand-to-generic table, and failing that the typed name in lower case.
- **RxNorm codes:** `rxnorm_ingredient` is set only when the search display has no strength, meaning the code is ingredient-level.
- **Status:** `stopped` and `taking` map to stopped and active. Text like "paused", "on hold" or "until" in the note or in how the patient takes it makes the row `held`.

- **Dose:** this is the strength times the count. "Morning" counts as one unit. An explicit amount in the patient's words, such as "20 units", wins. Ranges like "1 or 2", conditional directions and sliding scales get no dose.
- **Duplicates:** if the same ingredient appears twice, I emit one row and prefer a non-stopped entry.
- **Frequency:** inferred from the patient's wording, for example "morning and supper" is BID. Unclear wording like "most days" gets no frequency.
